newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks edge higher to fresh record.
newsitem.headline: French stocks edge higher to fresh record.

text.p: Paris shares scraped to a fourth consecutive record close on Monday although they finished well below their session highs.
Traders said foreign funds were entering the market, offsetting some profit-taking on the market's gains.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed up 0.93 point or 0.03 percent at 2,709.21. The CAC-40 futures contract was down two points at 2,715 from Friday's close.
* TF1 rises 6.54 percent to 570 francs. Societe Generale upgraded the stock to outperform from neutral after an upward revision to expected subscriptions to the TPS digital television service.
* Credit Lyonnais falls 5.56 percent to 204 francs on profit-taking, after recent speculative run up on hopes of yet another government bail-out.
* BNP sheds 1.82 percent to 264, as investors take profits after last week's strengthening on its 1996 results.
* Europe 1 drops after telling analysts it expects year results to stagnate at 70-80 million francs to end-decade.
* Groupe Zannier rises 5.93 percent to 175 francs amid rumours of a takeover of the textiles group.

* Groupe Andre gains 0.82 percent to 490 francs as the shoe store group starts on Tuesday a buyout offer for minority interest in Creeks unit, at 70 francs per share. Creeks was suspended today and resumes trading on Tuesday. It closed on Friday at 21.75 francs.
* Accor holds gains from last week, up 2.55 percent at 846, after Morgan Stanley's strong buy recommendation
* Promodes firms 3.21 percent, basking in afterglow of 1996 results, judged excellent by some.
